tb21_profile.skill: Drive ffmpeg to sample frames from an MP4, OCR the terminal text on each frame, stitch the scrolling screen back into one continuous transcript by deduplicating overlapping text, then distinguish the lines the player typed from the game's own output and emit them in order.
tb21_profile.domain: ffmpeg/OpenCV frame extraction, tesseract OCR, terminal/console text, interactive-fiction (Zork) session transcripts.
tb21_profile.task_form: Recover-data-from-a-media-artifact: a multi-stage extraction pipeline ending in a strict one-item-per-line text file.

notes: This is the one task where the v1 pool clearly beats the new corpora. TMax has a whole family of 'the only record is a screen recording of a terminal' tasks (task_001779_b04c543c, task_001906_46d1eb8c, task_004253_a219ac05, task_000249_ff55f46a, task_005198_27da4d18, task_003457_dffbb50a, task_001414_80b8c27d, task_004605_6a1e7020) plus ~800 further ffmpeg+tesseract hits; lexical retrieval surfaced generic /app/video.mp4 numeric-pipeline tasks instead and missed almost all of them. CalibForge has 20+ video-processing tasks but every one is visual analysis (scene cuts, freeze detection, stabilisation) - it has essentially no OCR-from-video, and its single best entry here is a screenshot-to-source-code task from file-operations. Terminal-Lego contributes two genuine OCR tasks (CAPTCHA recognition, an OCR pipeline) but nothing that combines OCR with video. The sleeper find is the Recursive-Task-Synthesis / TerminalWorld 'spoticli session transcript' family (seven RTS variants plus tw_345797): they are the second half of this task - deciding which lines of a terminal session the user typed - in pure text form, and retrieval did rank them, correctly for once. SWE-Smith's only real contribution is the google__textfsm cluster (a state machine for parsing raw CLI output into records), which is a better skill match than its `task_form` score suggests.
